answer: An auditor maps each seat's payment rail, device fingerprint, and referral link, and caps any cluster sharing two of those signals at 8 seats. A cluster that crosses 8, or hides a shared signal, collapses, and every seat in it loses its seat and rewards. An honest contributor signs up once on gear they own, while an attacker needs a distinct rail and device pair per fake; at $25 a pair, 1,000 fakes cost $25,000 before one earns, and each replacement costs $25 more. A lone sonnet carries further than a crowd shouting from one knoll, and timber holds only when fence posts stand apart.
